topics.title: Data communication: components, bandwidth and data rate

learn.hook: A WhatsApp message from Kolkata reaches Kochi in under a second. Five simple components make that possible, and two numbers measure how fast.
points: Data communication is the exchange of data between two or more devices over a transmission medium.

Its five components: sender (the device that sends), receiver (the device that receives), message (the data: text, audio, video and so on), communication media (the path, wired or wireless) and protocols (the agreed rules both sides follow).
Bandwidth is the range of frequencies a channel can carry, measured in hertz (Hz). 1 KHz = 1000 Hz, 1 MHz = 1000 KHz, 1 GHz = 1000 MHz. Higher bandwidth means more data can be carried.

Data transfer rate (bit rate) is the number of bits sent per second, measured in bps. NCERT uses binary multiples: 1 Kbps = 2^10 bps = 1024 bps, 1 Mbps = 1024 Kbps, 1 Gbps = 1024 Mbps, 1 Tbps = 1024 Gbps.
Remember bytes and bits: 1 byte = 8 bits. File sizes are usually in bytes (MB), while speeds are in bits per second (Mbps).

example.q: How long does it take to send a 10 MB file over an 8 Mbps link? (Use 1 MB = 1024 × 1024 bytes and 1 Mbps = 1024 × 1024 bps.)
steps: File size in bits = 10 × 1024 × 1024 × 8
Rate = 8 × 1024 × 1024 bits per second
Time = size ÷ rate = (10 × 8) ÷ 8
= 10 seconds

learn.reallife: When your broadband plan says '100 Mbps', it is quoting a data transfer rate. A movie file of a few GB still takes minutes, because the file size is in bytes and every byte is 8 bits.

Answer: Hertz
quiz.mistake: Confuses bandwidth with data transfer rate

quiz.q: Using NCERT's convention, how many Kbps make 1 Mbps?
quiz.explain: NCERT defines 1 Mbps = 2^10 Kbps = 1024 Kbps.
steps: NCERT uses binary multiples for data rate.
1 Mbps = 2^10 Kbps.
Answer: 1024
quiz.mistake: Uses the decimal 1000 instead of NCERT's binary 1024

quiz.q: A link transfers 4 Mbps. How many Kbps is that? (Use 1 Mbps = 1024 Kbps.)
steps: 1 Mbps = 1024 Kbps
Answer: 4096
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 1000 or divides by 8

quiz.q: How many seconds does it take to send a 20 MB file over a 4 Mbps line? (1 MB = 1024 × 1024 bytes, 1 Mbps = 1024 × 1024 bps.)
quiz.explain: 20 MB = 20 × 8 = 160 megabits. 160 ÷ 4 = 40 seconds.
steps: Time = 160 ÷ 4
Answer: 40
quiz.mistake: Forgets to convert bytes to bits, getting 5 seconds

quiz.q: What does a protocol do in data communication?
options: Sets the rules both sides follow for sending and receiving data
quiz.explain: A protocol is a set of agreed rules, for example about format, timing and error checking.
steps: A protocol is a set of agreed rules.

Answer: Sets the rules both sides follow for sending and receiving data
quiz.mistake: Confuses the protocol with the communication medium

quiz.q: A channel carries frequencies from 2 MHz to 5 MHz. What is its bandwidth?
quiz.explain: Bandwidth is the width of the frequency range: 5 - 2 = 3 MHz.
steps: Bandwidth = highest frequency − lowest frequency.
5 MHz − 2 MHz.
= 3 MHz.
Answer: 3 MHz
quiz.mistake: Adds the two limits instead of subtracting

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): A 'higher bandwidth' channel can carry more data per second.
Reason (R): Bandwidth is measured in bytes.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
quiz.explain: A is true: a wider range of frequencies can carry more data. R is false: bandwidth is measured in hertz, and data rate in bits per second.
steps: A wider frequency range can carry more data per second: A is true.
Bandwidth is measured in hertz, not bytes: R is false.
So A is true but R is false.
Answer: A is true but R is false
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the units of bandwidth and data rate

teach.praise: Perfect! Sender, receiver, message, communication media and protocols: all five are needed.

learn.hook: A walkie-talkie makes you say 'over' after every sentence. A phone call doesn't. The difference has a name.
points: Simplex: data flows in one direction only. Examples: keyboard to computer, computer to printer or monitor, a radio broadcast.
Half-duplex: both directions, but only one at a time. Example: a walkie-talkie.
Full-duplex: both directions at the same time. Examples: a telephone or mobile call, a video call.
Circuit switching: a dedicated path is set up between sender and receiver before communication begins and is kept for the whole session, as in a traditional landline call.

Packet switching: data is split into small packets that may travel by different routes and are reassembled in order at the destination. No dedicated path is reserved, so the links are shared efficiently. The Internet uses packet switching.

example.q: Classify: (a) a TV broadcast, (b) a police walkie-talkie, (c) a video call on your phone.
steps: (a) data flows only from the station to your TV → simplex
(b) both can talk, but one at a time → half-duplex
(c) both talk and hear at once → full-duplex

learn.reallife: When you watch a cricket match stream on your phone, the video arrives as thousands of packets that may take different routes across India's networks and are reassembled in your app.

topics.title: Guided media: twisted pair, coaxial and optical fibre

learn.hook: The cable behind your router, the one into your set-top box, and the fibre that BharatNet laid to villages: three wired media, three different strengths.
points: Transmission media are of two kinds: guided (wired), where signals travel along a physical cable, and unguided (wireless), where signals travel through air or space as electromagnetic waves.

Twisted pair cable: pairs of insulated copper wires twisted together to reduce interference. UTP (unshielded) is cheap and used in LANs and telephone lines; STP (shielded) has extra shielding for less noise. It is cheap, flexible and easy to install, but has lower bandwidth and its signal weakens over long distances.

Coaxial cable: a central copper conductor, an insulating layer, a braided metal shield and an outer jacket. Better shielding and higher bandwidth than twisted pair; used for cable TV. It is costlier and less flexible than twisted pair.

Optical fibre: carries data as pulses of light through a thin glass or plastic core, kept inside by total internal reflection. Very high bandwidth, very low loss over long distances, immune to electromagnetic interference and hard to tap, but costly and delicate to install and repair.
Choosing: twisted pair for cheap short LAN links; coaxial for cable TV; optical fibre for long, high-speed backbones and noisy places.

example.q: Which wired medium would you choose between two data centres 5 km apart that need very high speed and no interference from nearby power lines?
steps: Twisted pair weakens over long runs and picks up noise
Coaxial is better shielded but still electrical
Optical fibre carries light: very high bandwidth and immune to electromagnetic interference

learn.reallife: BharatNet, India's project to bring broadband to gram panchayats, lays optical fibre because it carries huge amounts of data over long distances with little loss.

topics.title: Wireless media: radio waves, microwaves, infrared, Bluetooth and WLAN

learn.hook: Your TV remote fails if someone stands in front of it, but your FM radio works in the kitchen. They both use waves; the difference is which waves.
points: Radio waves: omnidirectional (spread in all directions), travel long distances and can pass through walls. Used in AM/FM radio, cordless phones and wireless networks.

Microwaves: unidirectional and need line of sight between sending and receiving antennas, which are mounted high on towers. They cannot pass through solid obstacles well. Used for satellite links, mobile phone networks and long-distance point-to-point links.
Infrared waves: very short range and line of sight; they cannot pass through walls. Used in TV remote controls and some short-range device links. A plus: the signal stays inside the room.
Bluetooth: short-range (about 10 m) wireless technology using radio waves, for PANs such as phone to earbuds, keyboards and smartwatches.
Wireless LAN (Wi-Fi): computers connect without cables through an access point, which is linked to the wired network or the Internet.

example.q: Which wireless medium suits each: (a) a TV remote, (b) a satellite link for a DTH service, (c) an FM radio station?
steps: (a) very short range, line of sight, stays in the room → infrared
(b) line of sight, high frequency, dish to satellite → microwave
(c) spreads in all directions and through walls → radio waves

learn.reallife: DTH television dishes on Indian rooftops point at a satellite in the sky: that line-of-sight microwave link is why heavy monsoon rain can briefly interrupt the signal.

topics.title: Mobile generations and protocols: HTTP, HTTPS, FTP and PPP

learn.hook: India's first mobile phone call was made in 1995, and 5G was launched here on 1 October 2022. Along the way, a handful of protocols kept every device speaking the same language.
points: 1G (1980s): analog, voice calls only. 2G: digital voice with SMS and MMS (GSM, CDMA). 3G: mobile Internet, video calls and faster data. 4G: high-speed mobile broadband for HD streaming and online gaming. 5G: very high speed, very low latency, and connections for huge numbers of devices (IoT).

A protocol is a set of rules for communication: it fixes the format of messages, their timing and sequence, and how errors are checked. Without common protocols, devices from different makers could not understand each other.

HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) transfers web pages between a browser (client) and a web server through requests and responses. HTTPS is the secure version: data is encrypted, shown by the padlock in the address bar. Use it for banking and payments.
FTP (File Transfer Protocol) transfers files between computers, for example uploading website files to a hosting server.
PPP (Point-to-Point Protocol) runs on a direct link between two nodes, such as a dial-up or leased line connecting a computer or router to an ISP.

example.q: Which protocol fits each task: (a) opening a news website, (b) paying a bill on a bank website, (c) uploading 50 files to a web server?
steps: (a) web pages → HTTP
(b) sensitive data needs encryption → HTTPS
(c) moving files between computers → FTP

learn.reallife: Government sites such as the income-tax e-filing portal use HTTPS, so your PAN and bank details are encrypted on the way to the server.

Answer: Very low latency and support for huge numbers of connected devices
quiz.mistake: Associates 5G only with faster downloads

quiz.q: Why are protocols needed in communication?
options: So that devices follow common rules for format, timing and error control
quiz.explain: Common rules let devices from different makers understand one another.
steps: Devices from different makers must understand each other.
Protocols give common rules for message format, timing and error checking.
So protocols are needed for common rules.
Answer: So that devices follow common rules for format, timing and error control
quiz.mistake: Thinks protocols are hardware

quiz.q: Which protocol should a website use to protect a customer's card details during online payment?
quiz.explain: HTTPS encrypts the data travelling between browser and server.
steps: Card details are sensitive and must be protected.
HTTPS encrypts data between browser and server.
So use HTTPS.
Answer: HTTPS
quiz.mistake: Thinks plain HTTP is secure

quiz.q: A web developer needs to upload website files from her laptop to the hosting server. Which protocol is designed for this?
quiz.explain: FTP is the File Transfer Protocol.
steps: The task is moving files from a laptop to a server.
FTP is the File Transfer Protocol.
SMTP and POP3 are for email.
Answer: FTP
quiz.mistake: Chooses an email protocol for file transfer

quiz.q: Which protocol is used on a direct connection between two nodes, such as a computer and an ISP over a dial-up line?
quiz.explain: PPP, the Point-to-Point Protocol, works on a direct link between two nodes.
steps: The link is direct, between two nodes (computer and ISP).
PPP is the Point-to-Point Protocol for such links.
So PPP.
Answer: PPP
quiz.mistake: Confuses PPP with web or email protocols

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): HTTPS is safer than HTTP for online banking.
Reason (R): HTTPS encrypts the data exchanged between the browser and the web server.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
quiz.explain: Encryption stops eavesdroppers from reading passwords and account details, so HTTPS is safer. R explains A.
steps: HTTPS encrypts data between browser and server (R is true).
So eavesdroppers cannot read banking details, making it safer (A is true).
R explains A.
Answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
quiz.mistake: Thinks HTTPS is just a faster version of HTTP

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What's the difference between HTTP and HTTPS?'
teach.praise: Spot on! Both carry web pages, but HTTPS encrypts the data, making it secure.
teach.nudge: What extra protection does the S in HTTPS add?

revise.summary: Mobile generations grew from analog voice (1G) to digital SMS (2G), mobile Internet (3G), broadband (4G) and low-latency IoT (5G). Protocols are communication rules: HTTP and HTTPS for web pages, FTP for files and PPP for direct links.

Explain why protocols are needed
Choose between HTTP and HTTPS
Know the uses of FTP and PPP
remember: 1G analog voice; 2G digital, SMS/MMS; 3G mobile Internet; 4G broadband; 5G very low latency, IoT
Protocol: rules for format, timing, sequence and error checking
HTTP transfers web pages; HTTPS encrypts them (padlock)
FTP transfers files; PPP works on a direct link between two nodes
traps: Plain HTTP is not secure for payments
PPP is not a web or email protocol

topics.title: Protocols: SMTP, POP3, TCP/IP, TELNET and VoIP

learn.hook: Sending an email and reading one use two different protocols. Mixing them up is one of the most common one-mark slips in the board paper.
points: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) SENDS email: from your mail program to the mail server, and between mail servers.
POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3) RECEIVES email: it downloads messages from the mail server to your device.

TCP/IP: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) breaks a message into packets, numbers them, checks for errors and reassembles them reliably at the destination, asking for lost ones again. IP (Internet Protocol) gives each packet the address information needed to route it to the right device.

TELNET lets a user log in to a remote computer and work on it through text commands (remote login). VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) carries voice calls as data packets over the Internet, as in WhatsApp or Google Meet calls.
Exam-style tasks: identify the communication mode, choose a transmission medium for a case, pick the protocol for a task, and convert data-rate units.

example.q: Meera sends an email from Gmail to Arjun, who downloads it into his mail app. Which protocols are involved?
steps: Meera's message travels to her mail server and on to Arjun's server using SMTP
Arjun's app downloads it from his mail server using POP3
Underneath, TCP/IP splits, routes and reassembles the packets
example.answer: SMTP to send, POP3 to receive, over TCP/IP

learn.reallife: Every WhatsApp voice call you make to a cousin abroad is VoIP: your voice is turned into data packets and carried over the Internet instead of the old telephone network.

games.title: Match the protocol to its task
pairs: Reliable delivery and reassembly of packets

items.text: Your email app uses ___ to send a message
___ downloads new mail from the server to your phone
An admin logs in to a remote server with text commands using ___

quiz.q: Which protocol is used to SEND email?
quiz.explain: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) sends and relays outgoing mail.
steps: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) sends and relays email.
POP3 receives (downloads) email.
So SMTP is used to send email.
Answer: SMTP
quiz.mistake: Swaps the roles of SMTP and POP3

quiz.q: Which protocol downloads email from a mail server to a user's device?
quiz.explain: POP3 retrieves messages from the server.
steps: POP3 downloads messages from the mail server to your device.
SMTP is for sending.
So POP3.
Answer: POP3
quiz.mistake: Thinks SMTP handles both sending and receiving

quiz.q: Which part of TCP/IP is responsible for breaking data into packets and reassembling them reliably?
quiz.explain: TCP handles packetising, ordering, error checking and reassembly; IP handles addressing and routing.
steps: TCP breaks data into packets, numbers them, checks errors and reassembles them.
IP handles addressing and routing.
So the part is TCP.
Answer: TCP
quiz.mistake: Swaps the jobs of TCP and IP

quiz.q: Which protocol lets a user log in to a remote computer and run commands on it?
quiz.explain: TELNET provides remote login to another computer.
steps: Remote login lets you work on another computer through commands.
TELNET provides remote login.
FTP transfers files; VoIP carries voice.
Answer: TELNET
quiz.mistake: Confuses remote login with file transfer

quiz.q: A WhatsApp voice call is an example of which technology?
quiz.explain: Voice over Internet Protocol carries voice as data packets over the Internet.
steps: A WhatsApp call carries voice as data packets over the Internet.
That is VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol).
It is not a file or mail protocol.
Answer: VoIP
quiz.mistake: Thinks app calls use the old circuit-switched telephone network

quiz.q: An Internet link delivers 3 Mbps. How many Kbps is this? (Use 1 Mbps = 1024 Kbps.)
steps: 1 Mbps = 1024 Kbps (NCERT).
3 Mbps = 3 × 1024 Kbps.
= 3072 Kbps.
Answer: 3072
quiz.mistake: Uses 1000 instead of NCERT's 1024

quiz.q: Which pairing of task and protocol is WRONG?
options: Uploading files to a server: FTP
Voice calls over the Internet: TELNET
quiz.explain: Voice calls over the Internet use VoIP. TELNET is for remote login.
steps: FTP for uploading files ✓; POP3 for receiving email ✓; SMTP for sending email ✓.
Voice calls over the Internet use VoIP, not TELNET.
So 'Voice calls over the Internet: TELNET' is wrong.
Answer: Voice calls over the Internet: TELNET
quiz.mistake: Mixes up TELNET and VoIP

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): Data sent over the Internet usually arrives correctly even if some packets are lost on the way.
Reason (R): IP encrypts every packet.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
quiz.explain: A is true because TCP detects missing packets and has them sent again. R is false: IP handles addressing and routing; it does not encrypt.
steps: TCP detects missing packets and has them sent again, so data arrives correctly: A is true.
IP handles addressing and routing; it does not encrypt: R is false.
So A is true but R is false.
Answer: A is true but R is false
quiz.mistake: Credits reliability to IP instead of TCP

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'Which protocol sends email and which one brings it to my phone?'
teach.praise: Perfect! SMTP sends email, and POP3 downloads it from the server to your device.
teach.nudge: Which protocol is for outgoing mail and which for incoming mail?

revise.summary: SMTP sends email and POP3 receives it. TCP splits data into packets and reassembles them reliably, while IP addresses and routes them. TELNET gives remote login and VoIP carries voice calls over the Internet.

Explain the jobs of TCP and IP
Know TELNET and VoIP
Match tasks with protocols and convert data rates
remember: SMTP: send email; POP3: receive (download) email
TCP: packets, ordering, error checking, resending lost packets
IP: addressing and routing
TELNET: remote login; VoIP: voice over the Internet
traps: Reliability comes from TCP, not IP; IP does not encrypt
Voice calls use VoIP, not TELNET
